writeup: TIC 43712813 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 1.7056 days. The primary eclipse causes the system to dim by 6.12%, while no secondary eclipse has been detected. Automated analysis of TESS photometry data identified this candidate with a signal-to-noise ratio of 277.0, and pixel-level image analysis confirmed a peak signal-to-noise of 37.9, though the centroid offset of 3.9 arcsec suggests the signal may originate slightly away from the nominal target position. This candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a novel detection. The machine-learning pipeline assigned it a screening score of 0.59, indicating moderate confidence in its validity as a genuine eclipsing binary system.
